headline: Deep learning extracts nuclear and tissue features from histology and single-cell data
label: Deep Learning Histopathology Analysis
summary: January 2026 items extend deep learning to nuclear segmentation, tissue feature extraction, domain shift, and single-cell phenotype prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning applied to tissue and cellular data, with outputs tied to explicit histological, cellular, or clinical targets. FPNuNet segments and classifies nuclei in IHC images using a frequency-aware, prompt-guided network with four parallel encoders and multi-branch decoders. Histo-Miner extracts tissue features from H&E whole-slide images of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and releases new annotated nucleus and tumor-region datasets. scPhase applies attention-based multiple instance learning with a Mixture-of-Experts layer to predict sample-level clinical phenotypes from single-cell atlases. The preprint is distinct in addressing domain shift: a latent diffusion model conditioned on foundation-model features generates target-aware synthetic pathology images under semi-supervised domain adaptation. What is new is the emphasis on generative augmentation for domain shift and on task-specific architectural components, such as frequency-aware prompting and Mixture-of-Experts layers.
